o1.biggest_strength: It is a sprint-ready flow: the pause is flagged as the first thing to switch on because it carries 79% of the subscribers kept, with logging, a 10% holdout and legal review named.
o1.biggest_mistake: The 50%-off-for-switchers row counts 67 people as still paying at day 90 (the exact point 61% of discount takers leave) and values them at roughly full price, so about £600 a month of the gain is not really there.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Give an honest low/high range on the kept subscribers and either drop the switcher discount or model its cliff properly.

o2.biggest_strength: It separates what our own 2025 pause test proves (1,771 kept, 928 more than today's whole flow) from the two rows that are planning guesses, and sets a kill rule for them.
o2.biggest_mistake: There is no build order or sequencing for the sprint and no holdout, so the product team has to invent what to do first.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a week-one build order (pause first, then the plan switch, then the reminder) and a small control group to prove the lift.

reason: Both are usable and both correctly kill the blanket 50% off, but Output 1 is the one I can hand to the product team on Monday: it names the build order, the logging and a holdout, while Output 2 leaves me to work out what to build first. Output 2's numbers are the more honest of the two, so it is close.
